clue.text: Like Beckett's work to Mike, inhaling smoke in retreat

indicators.note: the word to takes in, as if breathing it, the reversed smoke
a retreating thing goes backwards, so the smoke is read right to left

parts.note: a cigar is a smoke
mike is short for microphone, also written mic

explanation.surface: An odd instruction about a play by Beckett being delivered to a man called Mike while he puffs away and backs off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mike' looks like a person's name, but it is the microphone. 'in retreat' gives RAGIC, which 'inhaling' puts inside TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Beckett's plays such as Waiting for Godot mix comedy with tragedy, a blend described by this adjective.

clue.text: Cecil is crazy, beginning to talk Latin, that is

indicators.note: crazy letters are deranged, so Cecil is gets rearranged
the beginning of the word talk is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone named Cecil seems to have lost his mind and is starting to speak in Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin adverb means 'namely' or 'that is to say', abbreviated sc. in scholarly writing.

clue.text: Daring copper ignoring melancholy

indicators.note: ignoring the melancholy word means leaving those letters out of the copper

parts.note: bluebottle is old British slang for a police officer, a copper
blue means sad or melancholy

explanation.surface: A police officer shows courage by shrugging off his low mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like the metal, but it is a policeman: BLUEBOTTLE, from the blue uniform. In British slang, having bottle means having nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses this word for nerve or courage, as in 'he lost his bottle'.

clue.text: Rhea's product, literally

indicators.note: read literally, a product of the letters of Rhea is something made from them, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A remark on what the Titaness Rhea produced, taken at its word.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Rhea was the mother of Hera, so the goddess is both her offspring and a reshuffle of her name's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hera, queen of the Olympian gods, was a daughter of Cronus and Rhea, so she is Rhea's offspring.

clue.text: Such vanity, writing about lying under daffodils!

indicators.note: in a down clue the writing lies under the flowers, so it comes after them

parts.note: daffodils belong to the genus Narcissus, plural narcissi

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: An exclamation at someone so vain they write about lying beneath the daffodils, a nod to Narcissus and Wordsworth.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive self-love and vanity is named after Narcissus, who fell in love with his reflection.

clue.text: Hummus maker, rustic wearing fancy cape

indicators.note: the rearranged cape is worn around the rustic, so it goes outside
fancy here means elaborately reworked, so the letters of cape are rearranged

parts.note: a hick is a rustic, an unsophisticated country person

explanation.surface: A country cook who makes hummus is dressed in an elaborate cape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' could describe the cape, but it is the anagram signal; the rearranged letters split round the rustic, as 'wearing' says.
explanation.definitionFit: Hummus is made from mashed chickpeas, so the legume is the ingredient that makes it.

clue.text: Setter's in a tuxedo, performing for neighbour

parts.note: DJ is short for dinner jacket, the British name for a tuxedo

indicators.note: the setter is in, placed inside the run of other pieces

parts.note: on means performing, as an actor on stage
Setter's is read as 'setter is', and the setter refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: The crossword setter is dressed in a tuxedo, performing on stage in place of the person next door.
explanation.definitionFit: To neighbour something, used as a verb, is to lie next to it, to border or abut it.

clue.text: Regularly miss receiving a Republican's spoils

indicators.note: the picked letters receive the next pieces, holding them inside
regularly means every other letter, taking the first and third of miss

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican in US politics

explanation.surface: A Republican's loot is regularly lost, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoil something is to blemish or ruin it, the same as marring it.

clue.text: Tommy's one holding sway over quiet period

parts.note: to rock is to sway back and forth
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
p is the musical marking piano, meaning quiet
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A soldier named Tommy keeps control through a quiet spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tommy' looks like a British soldier, but it is The Who's 1969 album, the best-known example of the form.
explanation.definitionFit: The Who's Tommy tells a story through a cycle of rock songs, making it an example of this genre.

clue.text: Stars taking part in noteworthy drama

indicators.note: taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Celebrities appearing in a remarkable stage play.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydra, the water snake, is the largest constellation, a group of stars in the southern sky.

clue.text: Pygmalion's work put away during social event

indicators.note: the eating happens during the event, so it goes inside it

parts.note: a gala is a festive social occasion
to put away food is to eat it, so ate

explanation.surface: Shaw's play is put aside while a party takes place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pygmalion' points to Shaw's play, but here it is the sculptor of myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the sculptor Pygmalion carved an ivory statue, later named Galatea, which came to life.

clue.text: Giant encyclopedias omitting various parts of Aeneid

indicators.note: omitting means the letters of Virgil's poem title are left out of the long word

parts.note: the six letters of the poem's title, A E N E I D, taken in whatever order they occur in the long word

explanation.surface: Huge reference works that leave out assorted passages of Virgil's epic.
explanation.walkthrough: The six letters of AENEID are removed one by one, not as a block, from ENCYCLOPEDIAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cyclops is the one-eyed giant of Greek myth, met by Aeneas and by Odysseus.

clue.text: Hoard cents and yen

parts.note: a yen is a longing, as is an ache

explanation.surface: Someone stockpiles American and Japanese money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yen' looks like the Japanese currency, but it is a longing.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden store of goods or valuables is a hoard, or stash.

clue.text: Pale individual in police department put off

parts.note: a pale is a stake or fence post

indicators.note: the individual goes in, inside the department

parts.note: one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A pale-faced person at the police station is unnerved.
explanation.definitionFit: To delay something to a later time is to defer it.

clue.text: He was bound to rock expert writer on the Guardian

parts.note: a pro is an expert
the setter calls himself me
this puzzle appears in the Guardian, which refers to itself as us

explanation.surface: A rock journalist was destined to write for this newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to rock' reads like destined for rock music; it means chained to a rock.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Titan who stole fire was chained to a rock in the Caucasus as punishment.

clue.text: They're used after passing entrance deck about noon

indicators.note: the entrance goes about the noon letter, around it

parts.note: a door is an entrance
a deck is a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Someone goes through a doorway with a pack of cards around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passing' looks like going by, but it means dying.
explanation.definitionFit: These cards record a wish that one's organs be given for transplant after death.

clue.text: Sit in a hot gloomy complex composing tales

indicators.note: complex means intricately tangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer sits in a hot, dismal, complicated place while writing stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning events into myths, the making of legends and tales, is the process meant.

clue.text: Old boys reportedly get to grips with a problem

parts.note: old boys are OBs, former pupils of a school

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word for getting to grips is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: to get to grips with a problem is to tackle it

explanation.surface: Former schoolboys are said to be dealing with a difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: A hindrance or barrier in one's way is a problem to overcome.

clue.text: Evil overcomes leader of Titans, like all the gods

indicators.note: in a down clue the evil word sits over and around the leader

parts.note: immoral means evil

indicators.note: the leader of Titans is its first letter

explanation.surface: Wickedness defeats the head of the Titans, as in the war of the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: Gods in myth never die; they are deathless, unlike mortals.

clue.text: Short piece about fuel returns in old sporting venue

indicators.note: the shortened piece goes about the fuel
short means cut, losing the last letter

parts.note: a column is a newspaper piece

indicators.note: returns means the fuel brand comes back, read backwards

parts.note: Esso is a brand of petrol, a fuel

explanation.surface: A brief article on fuel returning, set in an ancient arena.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' is a newspaper article, and the fuel is the Esso petrol brand; 'Short', 'returns' and 'about' act on them in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Rome's great amphitheatre hosted gladiator contests, an ancient arena for sport.

clue.text: What banks do about, for instance, celebrity

indicators.note: the bank activity goes about, around, the example abbreviation

parts.note: banks lend money
eg, exempli gratia, means for instance

explanation.surface: A riddle about what banks get up to with a famous person.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a famous person, a star renowned in their field.

clue.text: Woman's accepting order for old author

indicators.note: the woman accepts the order, holding it inside

parts.note: her means belonging to a woman
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A woman accepts an honour on behalf of an ancient writer.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek poet credited with the Iliad and Odyssey is a very old author.

clue.text: Dash to besiege Arab capital

indicators.note: the dash surrounds the Arab as a besieging army surrounds a town

parts.note: to hare is to dash, run fast
Ar is an abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

explanation.surface: A rush to surround an Arab city.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the capital city of Zimbabwe.

clue.text: Corner used to be hard for bunk

parts.note: to corner a market is to hog it, keep it to oneself
was means used to be
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A corner that once was hard for a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bunk' looks like a bed, but it is short for bunkum, nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunk, short for bunkum, means nonsense or rubbish.

clue.text: Old king doesn't finish idol

indicators.note: not finishing means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Herod was the king of Judea in the Bible

explanation.surface: An aged monarch fails to complete his idol.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is idolised and admired is a hero.

clue.text: Film game broadcast over part of Italy once

parts.note: ET is Spielberg's film E.T.
RU is rugby union

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the broadcast word is read backwards

parts.note: to air something is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A film about a game shown on TV, set in Italy long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient region of the Etruscans, roughly modern Tuscany, was a historic area of Italy.

clue.text: Collection of old poems mostly summed up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from bottom to top, backwards
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: summed means added

explanation.surface: A book of old verse mostly summarised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts ADDED to ADDE; 'up' turns it into EDDA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edda is a medieval Icelandic collection of Norse mythological poems.

clue.text: Right way back from waste processors

indicators.note: back means the way word is read backwards

parts.note: a lane is a way or road

explanation.surface: The correct route back from the recycling plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waste processors' sounds industrial, but it means the kidneys.
explanation.definitionFit: Renal means relating to the kidneys, the organs that filter waste from the blood.

clue.text: Deceptive foreign articles had inspiring name

parts.note: un is French for a and der is German for the

indicators.note: had breathes in the name abbreviation, taking it inside

explanation.surface: Dodgy imported goods carried a stirring name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' looks like goods, but means grammatical articles: French UN and German DER.
explanation.definitionFit: Underhand means sly or secret, done in a sneaky way.
